shared_qualifications: C1: conditional room-temperature saturated-KCl SCE comparisons. ALS/BAS lists +0.244 V versus SHE for saturated-KCl calomel and discusses 25°C reference operation (https://www.als-japan.com/2137.html); Corrtest lists +0.241 V versus NHE at25°C (https://www.corrtestinstruments.com/en/02437.html). C1a subtracts244 mV; C1b subtracts241 mV. Both are shown as alternative published comparison conventions, not paper uncertainty or constants fitted to CRA. Paper/CRA do not establish the physical calomel reference temperature/calibration. Numerical agreement is conditional on these25°C conventions; test-solution temperature is not assumed to be reference-electrode temperature. Identity uses alloy and test context independently.

PDF p.3 explicitly identifies Figure4 electrolyte as3%NaCl; p.4 gives distinct product/temperature markers. Four1150 mV points lie on the upper dashed line, whose meaning is not specified as censoring or no-pitting. Preserve the registered numerical readings; do not invent a bound.

Table2 supplies composition ranges and typical phases, not measured analyses of each plotted specimen. CRA fixed Cr/Ni/Cu/Mo numbers are range midpoints; duplex N=.1 represents a minimum and C=.08 a maximum, not established specimen analyses. Do not reconstruct exact source chemistry from CRA.

Cast20-type Table2 explicitly changes the N-column subheading to Nb and states Nb=8×%C; C maximum .07 implies .56 wt% Nb at that maximum, not .56 wt% nitrogen. CRA Nos.329–331 instead contain N=.56 and Nb=0.0. The source nitrogen content is unavailable. Independent designation, major-element ranges, austenitic phase and temperature identify these counterparts despite the field error.

Table3 lists1120°C solution treatment/water quench for these product classes as typical mechanical-property conditions. It does not independently establish treatment of each Figure4 pitting specimen; the common CRA treatment is not used to claim individual pitting-test provenance.

The cited nitrogen-added text comparison and high-N Figure1 endpoints (obs_002/005/008) can be related only tentatively to the30°C Ferralium255 row. Their exact named-product/specimen identity is not established. They remain candidate-only even though the converted potential agrees; no duplicate experiment or mean is asserted.

Obs_009/010 are pitting-current observations at imposed850 mV with unspecified electrode reference. Their upper bounds are not converted into exact thresholds or assigned to Figure4 records. Conventional18Cr10Ni3Mo temperature points have no matching alloy among the supplied CRA rows.
